author: Trash Theory
description:
Punk had a habit of getting up people’s noses. It was by design. It was a snotty in-your-face reaction to the status quo. The Stranglers embraced controversy like no other and were despised for it. Though getting attention around the same time, playing the same clubs, they ran counter to much of the new wave; musically competent, they took notes from progressive rock and The Doors, and had a destructive relationship with the press. There was an ugliness that ran through their music, their lyrical content and their actions. And yet they out-sold and out-lasted most of their punk contemporaries; as the 80s started their biggest hit was yet to come. This is New British Canon, and this is the Story of “Golden Brown”.
